thread:
ada: heads up 1 hitting a puzzling DX bug when importing the JS/TS SDK in an edge sample. Generics + chained overloads collapse to `any` after bundling/minify. Anyone else seen this?

ada: minimal repro in the sample app:
```ts
// sdk/src/chain.ts
export function mapItems<T, R>(items: T[], fn: (t: T) => R): R[]
export function mapItems(items: any[], fn: any) { return items.map(fn) }

// app/edge/worker.ts
import sdk from 'redwood-sdk' // default import used by sample
const out = sdk.mapItems(['a','b'], s => s.length) // used to be number[] but is now any[]
```

ron: interesting. our published package ships both an ESM entry and a tiny default-export wrapper for compatibility. Some bundlers will hoist/flatten that wrapper and break the link between the runtime file and the declaration file. TS ends up resolving to the wrapper which has poor or missing declarations.

maya: Are you publishing `types` only at root or also via `exports`? TypeScript prefers `exports.types` in modern resolution; missing that mapping can cause consumers to follow the runtime import path into a shim with no overloads.

ada: current package.json excerpt:
```json
{"main":"dist/index.cjs","module":"dist/index.mjs","types":"dist/index.d.ts","exports":{"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs"}}
```

ron: theres the problem 1 no `exports['.'].types`. Add it and ensure the ESM entry is the same module that contains the public typings (avoid re-export wrappers in separate files).

maya: another gotcha: some bundlers + minifiers mangle parameter names; if your d.ts generation is tied to compiled artifact names you can end up with mismatches. We generally generate `.d.ts` from source (tsc) and avoid post-build transform on types.

ada: quick test: switching the sample to `import { mapItems } from 'redwood-sdk'` (named import) restores inference. So import shape matters.

ron: short-term fixes:
- Add explicit `"exports": { ".": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs" } }`
- Remove default-export wrapper re-export file or have it re-export *from* the same module that contains the types (so TS resolution stays in one place).
- Add tsc --noEmit checks in our sample CI for `moduleResolution` set to both `node` and `bundler`.

maya: long-term: change packaging to emit a tiny `index.d.ts` next to runtime ESM shims and add a lint rule warning when `types` exists but `exports` lacks a types mapping. Also add a cookbook entry in onboarding: "Prefer named imports in edge samples until package `exports` includes `types` mapping".

ada: filed INF-8531 with a minimal esbuild bundle and repro (linked).

build-bot: CI: created branch `fix/exports-types-map` and ran tsc across samples on TS 5.0/5.1/5.2 1 failures reproduced on 5.1 only.

doc-bot: created doc draft: "Packaging & TS: exports/types patterns for ESM + Edge" in docs queue.

ron: follow-ups: add a small unit test in the SDK repo that asserts a couple of overload callsites still infer expected types post-packaging. That should catch regressions earlier.

maya: Ill draft the lint rule and the cookbook blurb. ada: thanks for a tight repro 1 will review your PR.
